sec: Hypertension 2023 · diagnosis, measurement protocol and secondary causes

items.q: Match each diagnostic modality with its cut-off on the table — 1) Office BP 2) Daytime ambulatory mean 3) Night-time ambulatory mean 4) Home BP mean … A) 135 and or 85 B) 130 and or 70 C) 140 and or 90 D) 135 and or 85
items.exp: Office and home values share nothing with the night-time row, which alone uses 130 over 70; daytime and home means are both 135 or 85, and the 24-hour mean is 130 or 80. (Book p978)

items.q: Which ambulatory measurement is bracketed as the best method for the diagnosis of hypertension?
items.exp: The row for the 24h mean carries the annotation best method for diagnosis of HTN, with cut-offs of 130 and or 80. (Book p978)

items.q: Assess the diagnostic sequence: I Ambulatory BP monitoring is the first choice, and office or home BP is used when it is not possible. II A single elevated reading above the diagnostic cut-off is enough to label confirmed hypertension.
items.exp: The flow starts with ABPM and falls back to office or home BP if that is not possible, and confirmation needs a mean of three readings followed by a repeat after one week. (Book p978)

items.q: How is the office measurement taken in terms of readings and interval, and how long before must coffee, cigarettes and exercise stop?
opts: 3 consecutive readings a minute apart, with 30 minutes of abstinence beforehand
2 readings five minutes apart, with 1 hour of abstinence
3 readings two minutes apart, with 15 minutes of abstinence
1 reading after 5 minutes, with no abstinence required
items.exp: The office protocol takes three consecutive readings at one-minute intervals after a 30-minute abstinence from coffee, cigarettes and exercise, with the patient seated comfortably for 3 to 5 minutes. (Book p978)

items.q: Fill up: In the office posture list the cuff is applied at ______ level, the arm is supported at the level of the ______, and the lower limb is kept ______.
opts: mid arm; heart; on the ground
items.exp: The four posture bullets are back rest, cuff at mid arm level, arm at the level of the heart and the lower limb on the ground. (Book p978)

items.q: After three office readings a mean of 148/92 mmHg is obtained at the first visit. What does the flowchart require next?
opts: Repeat the BP after 1 week and confirm if it is still at or above the cutoff
Order ambulatory monitoring before any repeat visit
items.exp: The office arm runs from the mean value at or above 140/90 to a repeat after one week and only then to confirmed HTN; the four-week interval belongs to the home BP arm. (Book p978)

items.q: How does the home BP arm differ in the interval before rechecking, and what equipment is acceptable for both arms?
opts: Recheck after 4 weeks; automatic electronic upper arm cuff or hybrid manual auscultatory devices
Recheck after 1 week; wrist devices only
Recheck after 4 weeks; mercury auscultatory devices only
Recheck after 24 hours; ambulatory devices only
items.exp: Home BP means a run of consecutive values, a mean at or above 140/90 and a recheck after 4 weeks, using either automatic electronic upper arm cuff devices or hybrid manual auscultatory devices. (Book p978)

items.q: Which element is NOT among the pre-measurement conditions for office BP on this page?
items.exp: The list covers comfortable sitting for 3 to 5 minutes, back rest, mid-arm cuff, arm at heart level, feet on the ground and 30 minutes free of coffee, cigarettes and exercise; an empty bladder is implied by good practice, not a full one. (Book p978)

items.q: Match each renovascular pattern with its clinical description — 1) Unilateral renal artery stenosis 2) Bilateral renal artery stenosis 3) Chronic glomerulonephritis … A) IgA nephropathy or membranoproliferative GN B) Normal renal function tests C) Renal failure with flash pulmonary oedema
items.exp: The types under renovascular disease read unilateral RAS with normal RFT and bilateral RAS with renal failure and flash pulmonary oedema, while chronic GN is specified as IgA or MPSGN. (Book p978)

items.q: Which of the following is not among the listed causes of renovascular hypertension?
items.exp: The three causes given are Takayasu, fibromuscular dysplasia and atherosclerosis; polyarteritis nodosa, though a vasculitis, is not listed. (Book p978)

items.q: Which three headings sit directly under rule out causes of secondary hypertension?
opts: Renal, coarctation of the aorta and obstructive sleep apnoea syndrome
items.exp: The renal and cardiac causes box branches into renal, coarctation of the aorta and OSAS; endocrine causes are given their own tree on the next page. (Book p978)

items.q: A 62-year-old smoker has sudden hypertension, a creatinine of 2.4 mg/dL and an episode of flash pulmonary oedema. Which entry of this page's secondary tree fits best?
opts: Renal renovascular disease with bilateral renal artery stenosis
Renal renovascular disease with unilateral renal artery stenosis
items.exp: The page assigns renal failure with flash pulmonary oedema to bilateral RAS, whereas the unilateral form is the one annotated with normal renal function tests. (Book p978)

items.q: Fill up: Under the renal heading the three branches are renovascular, ______ and chronic glomerulonephritis, and the abbreviation RAS is expanded on the page as ______.
items.exp: The renal branch splits into renovascular, thrombotic microangiopathy and chronic glomerulonephritis, and the legend printed at the bottom expands RAS as renal artery stenosis rather than the renin-angiotensin system. (Book p978)
